content.title: The Wild West Show
content.story: Before the trapeze artists and the lion tamers, the Wild West shows were the circus — trick riders, sharpshooters, and axe throwers who could bury a blade in a wooden target from twenty feet away without blinking. That tradition lives on here. Step up to the line. One throw at a time. Stick it.
content.challenge: Throw a tomahawk at a wooden target and try to stick it. Individual achievement recognized — best sticks and most consistent throwers recognized at the awards ceremony.
content.description: Each Scout gets a set number of throws (determined by station staff based on throughput). Scouts step to the throwing line, receive instruction from the station safety officer, and throw one tomahawk at a time. A 'stick' is a tomahawk that embeds in the target and holds without falling. Outstanding performers (most sticks in a session, clean rotation, best technique) may be recognized at the awards ceremony.
rules: All BSA Totin' Chip and tool safety guidelines apply
Station safety officer controls all throwing — no unsupervised throws
Only one Scout at the throwing line at a time
All others stand behind the designated safety line
No throwing until the safety officer gives the clear signal
No retrieving tomahawks until the safety officer gives the all-clear
Scouts must have Totin' Chip or receive brief safety orientation from station staff before throwing
content.time_and_scoring:
No formal scoring. Exhibition only.

Station staff may informally track sticks per Scout. Recognition at awards ceremony is at the discretion of the Camporee Director. Suggested award title: Top Axe Thrower.
content.setup: Establish a clear throwing range: throwing line, target line, and a roped-off spectator area behind and to the sides. Targets: 12–16 inch diameter logs or wooden rounds, set at an angle on a stand or staked into the ground. Standard throwing distance: 12–15 feet (adjust for rotation based on tomahawk weight). Have a certified or experienced BSA tool safety instructor lead this station.
content.reset: Collect all tomahawks before Scouts approach targets. Reset targets as needed. Estimated rotation: 2–3 minutes per Scout.
content.staffing: Minimum 2 adults: 1 safety officer/instructor at the throwing line, 1 to manage the queue and spectator area. Both should be experienced with tomahawk throwing and BSA tool safety.
content.supplies_text:
Tomahawks (balanced throwing hatchets): 3–5
Wooden targets (12–16 inch rounds): 3–4
Target stands or stakes: 3–4
Rope or tape for safety boundary: 50–100 ft
First aid kit: 1
Totin' Chip orientation checklist: 1
content.notes: This is an Exhibition event — no patrol or troop points. BSA does not sanction unsupervised tomahawk throwing — this station requires an experienced instructor and strict safety protocols. Practice throwing technique with station staff before the event. Award title suggestion: Top Axe Thrower, Sharpshooter.
